bib.title: DeepSeek-Prover-V2: Advancing Formal Mathematical Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning for Subgoal Decomposition

read.skipped: Appendix A/B/C example Lean proofs were read only in part (they are model outputs, not method).

question: Can a single LLM prover unify informal chain-of-thought reasoning and formal Lean 4 proof construction, using subgoal-decomposed synthetic cold-start data followed by RL with a binary verifier reward?
hypothesis: RL starting from a cold start of informal reasoning in task decomposition significantly enhances formal theorem-proving ability.
contributions: Recursive theorem-proving pipeline using DeepSeek-V3 for subgoal decomposition and a 7B prover for subgoals, producing cold-start CoT data
Curriculum learning with subgoal-derived conjectural theorems in expert iteration
GRPO stage with binary Lean-verified reward and an early consistency reward
DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B and 7B, with state-of-the-art results on miniF2F-test, PutnamBench and others
ProverBench: 325 formalized problems including 15 from AIME 24&25

method.summary: DeepSeek-V3 writes a natural-language proof sketch plus a Lean 4 skeleton of have-statements ending in sorry; a 7B prover solves each subgoal recursively, the subgoal proofs are composed and appended to V3's chain of thought as cold-start data. DeepSeek-V3-Base-671B is SFT'd on this plus expert-iteration non-CoT data, then trained with GRPO with binary Lean-verifier rewards; a 7B model is distilled and RL'd the same way.

datasets.name: Expert-iteration problem set (autoformalized plus Lean Workbook, STP synthetic, Goedel-Prover sets, and subgoal-derived problems)
datasets.split: miniF2F-valid used in curriculum; ProofNet-valid variants appear in the STP synthetic data used for SFT
datasets.source: Ying et al. 2024; Dong and Ma 2025; Lin et al. 2025
datasets.preprocessing: subgoals turned into two lemma types: (a) goal substituted, (b) preceding subgoals added as premises

datasets.name: Cold-start CoT data
datasets.source: problems the 7B prover cannot solve end to end but whose decomposed subgoals all resolve
datasets.preprocessing: composed formal proof appended to DeepSeek-V3's chain of thought

datasets.name: miniF2F
datasets.split: test for eval; valid used in curriculum
datasets.source: Zheng et al. 2022, revised version of Wang et al. 2025 plus two more valid revisions and one test revision

datasets.name: ProofNet
datasets.source: Lean 4 translation by Xin et al. 2024b

datasets.name: CombiBench
datasets.preprocessing: filtered for Lean 4.9.0 compatibility and multiple sorry placeholders

datasets.name: ProverBench
datasets.preprocessing: AIME: geometry, combinatorics and counting problems filtered out

models.name: DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B
models.context: 16,384 tokens in SFT; 32,768 max sequence in RL

models.name: DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B
models.init_from: DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5-Base-7B with context extended from 4,096 to 32,768 tokens

other.how: fine-tuned on rollouts from the 671B RL phase plus non-CoT expert-iteration data, then the same RL stage

other.use: subgoal decomposition and chain of thought
informal find-answer baseline on 15 AIME problems

training.objective: SFT, then GRPO with binary reward (1 if Lean verifies the proof, 0 otherwise) plus a consistency reward early in training that penalizes missing decomposed have-lemmas
training.batch_size: RL: 256 problems per iteration x 32 candidate proofs

other.rl_prompt_curation: only problems sufficiently challenging yet solvable by the SFT model
other.stage1: expert iteration in a curriculum to train the non-CoT model

inference.samples: Sample budgets 1 to 8192 per problem; mean and std over runs reported as mu +/- sigma (number of runs not stated)
inference.prompting: Two prompts: non-CoT ('Complete the following Lean 4 code' with Mathlib header) and CoT (same plus an instruction to give a detailed proof plan before the Lean code)

metrics.name: Pass@N
metrics.definition: fraction of problems with at least one Lean-verified proof in N samples

metrics.name: Problems solved
metrics.definition: count of benchmark problems solved (PutnamBench, CombiBench, AIME subset)

eval.protocol: Baseline numbers taken from original papers unless stated; STP on ProverBench run with open weights. Initial PutnamBench (49) and CombiBench (12) counts were later corrected after maintainers found misformulated statements.

prompts.text:
Complete the following Lean 4 code:
```lean4
import Mathlib
import Aesop
set_option maxHeartbeats 0
open BigOperators Real Nat Topology Rat
<docstring + theorem ... := by
  sorry>
```

prompts.purpose: CoT proof generation (suffix after the code block)
prompts.text: Before producing the Lean 4 code to formally prove the given theorem, provide a detailed proof plan outlining the main proof steps and strategies. The plan should highlight key ideas, intermediate lemmas, and proof structures that will guide the construction of the final formal proof.

limits: No ablation of the consistency reward, the cold start, or the subgoal curriculum; the paper states the consistency reward 'enhances proof accuracy' without a number.
Optimizer, GRPO hyperparameters (clip, KL, reward weights), number of RL steps, hardware and compute are not given.
Cold-start set is only 'hundreds' of examples; data sizes for expert iteration are not given.
The number of runs behind the +/- std values and decoding settings (temperature, top-p) are not stated.
miniF2F-valid is in the curriculum, so valid scores are not held-out; miniF2F was also revised by the authors, so numbers are not directly comparable to versions used by baselines.
Baseline numbers come from the original papers, not a shared harness; sample budgets differ across methods.
The AIME comparison mixes tasks: the prover is handed the answer, DeepSeek-V3 must find it.
Early versions over-counted PutnamBench (13 problems via an apply? bug in Lean 4.9.0) and CombiBench (12 vs 10), which the authors corrected.
Future work: scale to an AlphaProof-like system for IMO-level problems.
